title: Aside vs Dia Browser: Which One Does the Work for You?
summary: Aside vs Dia browser, compared using each company's documentation, Aside's shipped code and 85 public user posts: actions, desktop apps, data, pricing, limits.
body_markdown:
The Arc browser shuts down on December 22, 2026, and The Browser Company is moving Arc users to Dia ([TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/arc-browser-sunsets-december-22-as-the-browser-company-doubles-down-on-dia) , Oct 22, 2026). You may be trying Dia now, or already using it. Its AI reads and writes for you. It gives you a morning brief, answers questions about your open tabs, and drafts reports and slides. Work that runs across several websites is still yours. You open the vendor portal, find this month's invoices and download them yourself.


Aside is a browser that does that part for you. Tell its agent what you want done, and it opens the sites you are already signed in to, clicks through them and finishes the job. It also works in the apps on your computer, where it[ranked #1 in a benchmark run by Scale](https://aside.com/blog/aside-computer-use-ranks-number-one-in-cua-driver-bench) .


So which should you use? Use Dia if you want AI that reads, answers and drafts. Use Aside if you want the browser to do the task itself, across websites and in the desktop apps on your computer.


Aside and Dia compared: what the AI does, moving between sites, desktop apps, sign-ins, the free plan and using your own AI plan.


## How did we compare Aside and Dia?#


We read each company's own documentation on November 19, 2026, checked every Aside claim against the code of its current release, and collected 85 public first-hand posts and reviews: 42 about Dia and 43 about Aside. We also gave Aside six tasks that Dia users said Dia could not do.


Evidence Dia Aside


Product documentation Home, pricing, security, apps, changelog and release notes Help center, pricing and changelog, plus the code of release 1.26.1118


First-hand posts and reviews we could verify 42: 19 positive, 17 negative, 6 mixed 43: 15 positive, 21 negative, 7 mixed


Where they came from Hacker News, Reddit, X and hands-on reviews G2, Product Hunt, Hacker News, Reddit, X and independent reviews


## What is the difference between Aside and Dia?#


Dia is a browser with an AI that reads and writes. It briefs you each morning and builds answers, reports and decks from your tabs and the apps you connect. Aside is a browser with an agent that acts. It signs in, clicks and types on the sites you use, and hands you the finished result.


Each row is from the product's own documentation.


Capability Aside Dia


Acts on the page Clicks, types, fills forms and downloads in your signed-in tabs Fills forms and drafts email after you approve the content


Moves between sites on its own Yes No. Its agent is "unable to navigate on its own to another website"


Signs in for you Aside Vault fills saved logins. The agent does not receive the password Password fields are "invisible to the agentic system"


Works with your other apps Uses each site the way you would Connected apps. It can write back to Notion and create or edit Figma files


Repeat work Routines you schedule, run on your computer while it is awake A daily Morning Brief. No general scheduler is documented


Model choice Aside's models, your ChatGPT, Claude, GitHub Copilot or Grok plan, an API key, or a local model GPT, Claude and Gemini, chosen by Dia. No model picker or own-plan option is documented


Memory Markdown files on your computer that you can open and edit Its memory feature is being retired (changelog, Sep 24, 2026). Chat searches past chats and history on request


Runs on macOS 15 or later, Windows 10 22H2 or Windows 11 macOS and Windows


A routine can be as small as[answering Instagram comments that ask for a link](https://aside.com/blog/free-manychat-alternative-instagram-comment-link) . Dia is also one of eight browsers in our[feature-by-feature comparison of AI browsers](https://aside.com/blog/best-ai-browsers) .


## Can Dia do tasks for you, or does it only answer questions?#


It does more than answer, inside limits it documents. Dia can fill in a form or draft an email once you approve the content, and it can write to Notion and Figma through connected apps. Its security page says its agent is "unable to navigate on its own to another website."


Two November Dia browser reviews tested it. In[ZDNET](https://www.zdnet.com/innovation/dia-ai-browser-hands-on) (Nov 15, 2026), Jack Wallen built a Dia skill to summarize five open tabs and found it "100% successful at summarizing the content of all open tabs." In[How-To Geek](https://www.howtogeek.com/i-switched-from-chrome-to-dia-for-a-week-and-heres-what-stood-out) (Nov 9, 2026), Nimrah Chaudhry had Dia find information and draft an email: "All that's left is to send the draft." Her calendar test went differently: "It could tell me what was on my schedule, but it couldn't create an event. Instead, it provided a template and steps for doing it myself."


[Sam Nesler](https://samnesler.com/posts/arc-zen-dia-aside) , who tested both browsers (Aug 9, 2026), wrote: "Dia is an assistant. It reads your tabs, summarizes, drafts, and writes, but it fundamentally does not act on your behalf."


## What happens when Aside gets the tasks Dia users say it can't do?#


Aside finished all six. We collected six tasks that Dia users and reviewers said Dia could not do, from September to November 2026. Then we gave each one to Aside on November 19 and 20, 2026. Every run took under 2 minutes.


Start with an apartment search. In September,[a Dia user on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/diabrowser/comments/1w7svd8/is_dia_ai_tabs_integration_even_that_good/) wanted Dia to add each listing he liked to a spreadsheet, with the link, location, price per square foot and distance from work. He wrote: "Dia struggles to extract the listing URL correctly and refuses to populate the spreadsheet." We gave Aside the same job for one listing. It found a one-bedroom in San Francisco and added a row with the link, location, rent, size, price per square foot and distance from work to a new Google Sheet in 1 minute 51 seconds.


The apartment listing Aside added to a Google Sheet, Nov 20, 2026


The other five tasks come from two reviews. Nimrah Chaudhry tried a calendar event for How-To Geek, and[BenchTested](https://benchtested.app/apps/dia/) tried four more tasks (Oct 28, 2026). Each reviewer reported that Dia couldn't do the task. Aside did each one:


Task Aside What the reviewer reported


Create a calendar event Created it in 24 seconds "it couldn't create an event"


Fill in and send an order form Sent it in 22 seconds "I can't type into fields, click buttons, or send a form"


Fill in a form with a date picker and dropdowns Sent it in 26 seconds "I can't type into fields, pick from dropdowns or click buttons"


Set up a task that runs every weekday at 9 AM Set it up in 1 minute 43 seconds "I can't schedule this to run on its own"


Buy a product on a demo shop Checked out in 28 seconds Dia "said it cannot click buttons or check out"


BenchTested tested Dia on Windows with a free account and did not publish its exact prompts, so we wrote our own. Dia's security page says it can fill a form after you approve it, so Dia may do more on a Mac or a paid plan than BenchTested saw.


## What do people say Aside actually gets done?#


Users name finished errands: a cited Google Sheet, a canceled Verizon line, booked comedy shows. Of the 43 Aside posts, 21 discuss the agent's work: 13 positive, 4 negative and 4 mixed. Their words are below, including a mistake the agent made and a page it had to read twice.


[Michael Wilson](https://michaelawilson.co/aside-ux-audit) , in an unsolicited audit on Windows (October 2026), gave the agent one job, comparing Figma, Framer and Webflow pricing in a Google Sheet: "Twelve minutes later I had a cited, four-tab Sheet in my own Google account."[William Chen](https://www.producthunt.com/products/aside-6/reviews) listed on Product Hunt what it did in about six weeks, starting with: "Dealt with Verizon support, canceled my unused watch line, and gotten me another $120/year off my bill." He also reports an auto-renew mistake the agent made and then cleaned up, and says he considered Dia before choosing. In another Product Hunt review, Basal John notes that some pages "can take a second snapshot attempt before resolving dynamic elements."


Nesler wrote "Aside is an agent" and listed what it did for him: "research flight transfer times, draft emails, find and book comedy shows, and fill out the rote parts of job postings."


Our own run, on November 16, used this prompt:


> On LinkedIn, open the Aside page (linkedin.com/showcase/asidehq) and collect its 5 most recent posts: date, the first 80 characters, reactions and comments. Save them as aside-linkedin-posts.csv and show me the table. Read only: don't react, comment, follow or message anyone, and keep it to three page loads or fewer.


Aside's task view after collecting the latest posts from Aside's LinkedIn page, Nov 16, 2026


It returned the table in chat and saved the CSV. The agent runs[in your own signed-in browser](https://aside.com/blog/ai-agent-that-doesnt-get-blocked) , so it starts from the logins you already have.


We also read 22 X posts from people who tried both browsers. Sixteen come from a file of praise we keep.[Prasoon](https://x.com/MadebyPrasoon/status/2089434469044543597) (Aug 17, 2026) had been "using Dia from more than a year and never understood what it's AI was for because it literally does nothing."[Daniel F](https://x.com/mrdanielfeo/status/2119667655670153254) (Nov 8, 2026) moved over for "agentic capabilities especially around Figma and building prototypes."


## How do Aside and Dia differ in everyday use?#


Some people who tried both call Dia the more polished browser and Aside the stronger agent. They also differ on control. Dia stops before anything irreversible, and Aside sends or submits unless you turn on a confirmation step. The quotes below are from users and from each company's pages.


**Where the effort goes.** On Hacker News,[falloon](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50198096) (Oct 22, 2026) wrote of Dia: "it's a well designed and thoughtful UX."[Koller](https://x.com/0xKoller/status/2116276825924018429) (Oct 30, 2026): "dia browser is constantly pushing you to use the chat instead of doing its job."[arush](https://x.com/arcinston/status/2120238600545829096) , who tried both (Nov 10, 2026), found Aside "a bit clunky comparing it to dia in terms of product finish" and added "cua on aside is really good," meaning Computer Use.[Conrad](https://x.com/conradsbx1/status/2120645701453644263) (Nov 11, 2026), on Aside: "their ai stuff is like very insanely very good the browser itself is just kinda decent."[Günther](https://x.com/gunta85/status/2097315059328545044) (Sep 8, 2026) switched from Dia to Aside: "Best browser UX I've used, and snappy in a way nothing else is." His wishlist begins: "One account, all profiles."


Mike of HTML All The Things on X, Sep 1, 2026


**Speed and memory.** In the ZDNET review, Wallen called Dia "one of the fastest AI browsers I've used."[Daniel Zolfaghari](https://x.com/dzlgfcb/status/2103439400709595377) (Sep 25, 2026) wrote that Dia "has become much more less performant in the last couple of months." On Aside,[sammykins](https://x.com/thesammykins/status/2090022413191074277) (Aug 19, 2026): "it's been snappy, not a hog on resources for no reason." Nesler "ran out of memory with only 10 tabs visible." Aside's[changelog](https://docs.aside.com/changelog/native) now lists Memory Saver as on by default, which discards inactive tabs to free memory.


sammykins on X, Aug 19, 2026


**What you pay for.** One Dia user wrote on[Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/diabrowser/comments/1xdb5k8/dear_dia_team_please_dont_make_the_same_mistakes/19rjlblz722px/) (Oct 23, 2026): "as soon as you use it three times for free it just pops up an upgrade page. I already pay directly to a few AI companies. I'm not adding another." On Aside,[Usmaan](https://x.com/usmaanrzq/status/2114789070538678423) (Oct 26, 2026): "I like that I can bring my AI subs for better AI usage within the browser." Wilson's 12-minute task "used about 145 of the month's 500 free credits, or 29%."


**Who presses send.** Dia's security page says it "won't take irreversible actions on behalf of the user" and that calendar events "stay in draft until you click" Create. Basal John, on Aside: "When it needs a decision or an approval before sending or submitting, it alerts you." Chen: "I still have to step in sometimes, but it's already become my default way of getting things done." On the defaults, Wilson asked the agent to email his own address and it "sent it, with no prompt. With Final confirm on, the same request stopped at a card showing the full email, with Cancel and Confirm." Final confirm is off by default. Turn it on for anything that spends money or speaks in your name.


## How do Aside and Dia handle your logins and data?#


Both send your prompt and page content to an outside AI provider, unless you pick a local model in Aside. Both say your chats and history are stored on your computer. Dia routes requests through Atlassian's AI Gateway and hides password fields from its agent. Aside fills saved logins without showing the agent the password.


From each company's security and help pages:


Aside Dia


Where a request goes The task runs on your computer. The model you pick receives the task's context "through our servers and Atlassian's AI Gateway to our AI providers"


Stays on your computer Chats, task history, memory, routines and settings "your conversations, history, bookmarks, and files are encrypted and stored locally"


Account Aside account Atlassian account


One correction to Nesler's review: it says Aside runs routines "on their servers in the cloud." Aside's[help center](https://docs.aside.com/help/devices) says routines run on your own computer, and that cloud handoff is not available yet.


## Can Aside or Dia work in your desktop apps?#


Aside can. Computer Use lets its agent open and work in the desktop apps on your Mac or Windows PC, outside the browser, and it is available on every plan. In Cua Driver Bench, a test run by Scale, Aside Computer Use ranked #1 and passed 88 of 90 trials. Dia's product pages document no feature for controlling desktop apps.


[Cua Driver Bench](https://huggingface.co/spaces/earakely-scale/CuaDriverBench-AgentEnv) checks whether an AI agent can finish real office tasks across desktop apps without disturbing someone working on the same computer. With Claude Opus 5.5, Aside Computer Use scored 97.8%. Cua Driver scored 74.4%, Codex Computer Use 51.1% and agent-desktop 47.8%. Scale ran every tool through the same coding agents on macOS, so the score reflects the computer-use tool itself. Dia was not in the test.


Cua Driver Bench results by Scale


Scale ran this benchmark, not Aside. Aside's browser-agent scores come from[its own runs](https://aside.com/blog/how-we-built-the-sota-browser-agent-that-outperforms-fable) , and Nesler notes that they "haven't been reproduced."


On a Mac, Aside does most of this in the background, so you can keep working while it runs. Aside reports that with Claude Sonnet 5.5 it passed 37 of 40 background trials without disturbing the user. On Windows, it brings the app to the front and takes the mouse and keyboard while it clicks and types.


Turn it on in Settings > Agents, then start a task and name the app. It does not run in scheduled routines or incognito tasks.


Computer Use in Settings > Agents


## How much do Aside and Dia cost?#


Aside's free plan includes the agent, with 500 credits a month, and lets you connect a ChatGPT or[Claude subscription you already pay for](https://aside.com/blog/aside-vs-claude-in-chrome) . Dia's free plan is a browser with no AI features after a 14-day trial. Paid plans are $20 and $200 a month for Aside, and $10 and $100 a month for Dia.


Plan by plan, from[aside.com/pricing](https://aside.com/pricing) and Dia's pricing page on November 19, 2026:


Aside Dia


Free Agent included. Up to 3 active routines and a built-in password manager "A better browser, without the AI"


Trial None needed 14 days of Better Days. After that, AI features pause until you pick a paid plan


First paid plan Pro, $20 a month: "3x Free usage," Ultrabrowse for deep research, unlimited routines, Channels Better Answers, $10 a month: Morning Brief, ask Dia, connected apps


Top plan Max, $200 a month: "40x Free usage" Better Days, $100 a month: "20x more asks"


Extra usage Add-on credits that do not expire $20 credit blocks that last up to three months


Dia's pricing page says its paid plans are "starting with new Mac users," that existing users "keep what they have for free" for now, and that "Dia on Windows stays as it is for now."


## Dia vs Arc: is Aside a good Arc browser alternative?#


Users like[rishi](https://x.com/thelifeofrishi/status/2069587284014309681) say so: "tried Aside, might switch from Arc!" (Jun 23, 2026). Aside has a sidebar with vertical tabs, pinned tabs and split view, and it can import from Arc on Mac and Windows. Dia is Arc's official successor and imports your Arc setup too. Users of both still ask for Arc features such as Peek.


Pinned tabs and bookmarks in Aside's sidebar


Arc migration is the most discussed topic in the Dia posts: 6 positive, 7 negative and 4 mixed. On Hacker News,[jhaile](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50199454) (Oct 22, 2026): "The main features I miss from Arc are Peek, Air Traffic Control, and Nested Folders." Dia added nested tab groups in November.[parth](https://x.com/parthsareen/status/2118492924484952332) (Nov 5, 2026): "switched to using dia now. the biggest thing i miss right now is little arc."


From an Aside user,[André Pinto](https://x.com/aPinix/status/2121929263947370556) (Nov 15, 2026): "I need Peek and Mini Aside in order to make it my daily driver."


Aside uses profiles where Arc had Spaces. Each profile keeps its own history, bookmarks and logins. rishi's reasons included "this has the autonomy no other browser I've tried has" and "has Arc aesthetics."


## How do you switch from Dia to Aside?#


Download Aside for Mac or Windows, sign in, and choose Dia on the import screen. Aside lists what it will bring over: browsing history and cookies, extensions, pinned tabs and bookmarks, saved passwords, addresses, payment cards and browser settings. Then open a new tab, select Ask and enter your first task.


Aside's import screen with Dia selected, Nov 19, 2026


The Import from Dia screen, Nov 19, 2026


If Aside finds more than one Dia profile, choose the one you want to import. You can also import later from Settings > General. Set up Aside Vault next, so the agent can sign in for you ([Get started](https://docs.aside.com/help/get-started) ).


### Questions Dia users ask#


**Can I limit what the agent is allowed to do?**


Yes. Every task has a[permission mode](https://docs.aside.com/help/security) . Read only lets it read without changing your files. Guard is the default: it works in folders you approve and asks before it touches others. Full access lets it read and write anywhere on the computer.


**Can I message the agent when I am away from my computer?**


Yes, on Pro and Max. Channels let you start and steer tasks from Slack, Telegram or Discord while Aside runs them on your computer.


**Can I run a task without my logins?**


Yes. Start it in Incognito mode. The task browses without your normal browser profile, and agents cannot use saved Vault logins there.


**Can Claude Code or Codex use Aside?**


Yes. Aside includes a command-line tool and an MCP server, so another agent can drive the browser. Setup is in the[developer guide](https://docs.aside.com/help/developers) .


See what the[browser agent](https://aside.com/features/browser-agent) can do, then[download Aside](https://aside.com/download) for Mac or Windows.
